issue_context.summary: FancyZones Override Windows Snap was enabled in settings but inactive after startup until toggled off and on; a later report says it could also stop randomly.
known_information: The original report is on PowerToys 0.67.1 and portrait monitors.
Toggling Override Windows Snap restores the hotkey behavior.
Current FancyZones UI coverage explicitly restarts PowerToys with overrideSnapHotkeys enabled and asserts Win+Arrow zones a window.
inferences: The original startup-order bug may now be fixed; any current failure may instead be a hook loss or a configuration-specific startup race.
issue_context.analysis: A current test covers the basic persisted-setting restart case, so the next evidence must establish whether a latest release still fails and whether it is startup-only or a later hook loss. A focused settings export avoids requesting unrelated diagnostics.
initial_investigation: FancyZones.UITests.Next/CoreBehaviorTests.cs restarts PowerToys after enabling Override Windows Snap and asserts zone cycling.
No pull request referencing issue 24198 was found.

comment.body:
Thanks for documenting that toggling **Override Windows Snap** restores Win+Arrow behavior and that the failure affected portrait displays. Current FancyZones main now has a restart test for the persisted setting, so we need to know whether a released build still fails or whether the remaining case is a later hook loss.

**Needed**
1. Please retest after a full Windows sign-out or reboot on the latest stable PowerToys release and provide the version from About.
2. If it fails, please share only the relevant FancyZones settings/export or screenshots showing Override Windows Snap, the active portrait-display layout, and move-across-monitor options, with personal paths removed.

This will distinguish startup settings loading from hotkey-hook or layout routing failure.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep Override Windows Snap active across startup and hook recovery
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Best current hypothesis: the persisted setting can be loaded before the keyboard hook is ready, or the hook can later be lost without reapplying the enabled routing state.
plan: Trace setting load, FancyZones startup, and Win+Arrow hook registration/recovery order.
Make hook activation idempotently reflect the latest persisted setting after startup and any hook reinstall.
Extend restart coverage to Windows sign-in timing, portrait layouts, and simulated hook loss.
verification: Reboot/sign in repeatedly with Override Windows Snap enabled and verify the first Win+Arrow after startup uses the active FancyZones layout without toggling settings.

confidence.rationale: The toggle workaround suggests state application, but current tests imply the original basic path may already be fixed.
